candidates.attacker_control: Attacker controls the request to POST /api/1/services/api/1/deployment/bulk-golive.json: site_id, environment (e.g. the live target), path (subtree root, typically '/'), and comment. Any authenticated Studio account can send it, whether or not the user is a member of the target site and whether or not the user has the 'publish' permission (no @HasPermission and no voter covers this path).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for other permission enforcement on the traced path: (a) no @HasPermission annotations exist anywhere in org.craftercms.studio.api.v1 interfaces or on v1 DeploymentServiceImpl/DmPublishServiceImpl methods; (b) the SitePolicyAspect (@ValidateAction) only evaluates site content policy (path/type/size), it performs no user-permission check and is bypassed for create-folder by internal self-invocation (validateAndCreateFolder calls this.createFolder); (c) revert-content is partially mitigated because v1 ContentServiceImpl.revertContentItem first calls contentServiceV2.lockContent, and the v2 ContentServiceImpl.lockContent does carry @HasPermission(content_write) - so the revert path was excluded from the claim; change-content-type is also excluded because the v1 path throws 'Unexpected code path' and its lockContent resolution is the v1 service; (d) write-content.json is explicitly mapped to content_write and the v1 writeContent methods carry @HasPermission, so the classic write path is not affected; (e) the v2 REST controllers/services (publish, content create/rename) do enforce the expected permissions, showing that the legacy v1 path is the outlier; (f) security header/CSP settings are irrelevant here.
candidates.impact: Unauthorized publication: an authenticated user without the publish permission (and without site membership) can force the queuing, and thereby the publication, of the target site's pending modifications to a configured environment such as live, bypassing the publish permission and any peer-review/approval workflow. This is an integrity/defacement and potential information-exposure issue (unreviewed or malicious sandbox content pushed to production). Related same-root-cause impact: read-only site members can create folders and rename/move files and folders (assets, scripts, templates, files) in the sandbox repository.
candidates.prerequisites: A valid authenticated Studio session (any account, including a user with no membership in the victim site); a valid target site id and a configured publishing target/environment; the target site must have pending (unpublished) changes for anything to be queued. No special permission is required.
candidates.root_cause: Legacy API 1 authorization is enforced only by URL-scoped access-decision voters: StudioContentAPIAccessDecisionVoter only considers URIs starting with /api/1/services/api/1/content/ and StudioPublishingAPIAccessDecisionVoter only considers /api/1/services/api/1/publish/ (and only special-cases the exact .../publish/commits.json URI). All other /api/1/** URIs fall through to the plain isAuthenticated() rule (security/api.xml lines 102-103). The v1 service methods reached by these scripts (DeploymentServiceImpl.bulkGoLive/deploy, DmPublishServiceImpl.bulkGoLive and v1 ContentServiceImpl.createFolder/renameContent) have no @HasPermission annotations (unlike their v2 counterparts, e.g. v2 PublishServiceImpl.publishAll/publish-by-commits and v2 ContentServiceImpl.renameContent/lockContent), and no service-internal permission check. The legacy Groovy REST scripts and SpringService wrappers perform parameter-format validation only and then call these beans directly.
candidates.title: Missing authorization on legacy Studio API 1 deployment endpoint allows any authenticated user to queue a site for publishing (bulk-golive)
candidates.trace: 1) Security chain for /api/1/** (security/api.xml 85-104) permits all public URLs, otherwise only requires isAuthenticated(); the two Studio voters abstain for this URI because it is neither under /api/1/services/api/1/content/ (StudioContentAPIAccessDecisionVoter 56-60) nor under /api/1/services/api/1/publish/ (StudioPublishingAPIAccessDecisionVoter 66-69, which only checks .../publish/commits.json, 88-104). 2) bulk-golive.post.groovy reads site_id/environment/path/comment and validates only that site is non-empty (20-51), then calls DeploymentServices.bulkGoLive (49). 3) SpringDeploymentServices.bulkGoLive looks up bean 'cstudioDeploymentService' (39-42), which is wired to the v1 org.craftercms.studio.impl.v1.service.deployment.DeploymentServiceImpl (studio-services-context.xml 148-168). 4) v1 DeploymentServiceImpl.bulkGoLive (417-424) performs only @ValidateStringParam/@ValidateSecurePathParam checks and delegates to DmPublishServiceImpl.bulkGoLive (107-155, no @HasPermission), which gathers all changed items under the subtree via itemServiceInternal.getChangeSetForSubtree and calls deploymentService.deploy for each. 5) v1 DeploymentServiceImpl.deploy (105-183, no @HasPermission) updates item publish state, builds publish requests and persists them via publishRequestMapper.insertItemForDeployment (164-168), then sets the site publishing status to QUEUED (177-181), which the Studio publisher processes. The same authorization gap exists for legacy content write operations: StudioContentAPIAccessDecisionVoter grants every /content/ URI except the exact write-content.json with only content_read (78-82), while v1 ContentServiceImpl.renameContent (2658-2672, moves/commits content), createFolder/validateAndCreateFolder (697-743) have no @HasPermission, so a read-only site member can create or rename content through create-folder.json/rename-folder.json.
candidates.unverified: Static review only; no code, server, or request was executed. Not runtime-confirmed. Unverified assumptions: (1) the Crafter Engine REST script controller maps /api/1/services/api/1/deployment/bulk-golive.json to scripts/rest/api/1/deployment/bulk-golive.post.groovy as the file layout and crafter.urlMappings suggest; (2) Spring AOP actually applies the @Valid/validation annotations but not any hidden permission aspect on the v1 beans; (3) the queued publish requests are subsequently processed by the publishing job into a live/preview target (publishing may be gated by the per-site 'publishing enabled' flag and publisher cron configuration); (4) for bulk-golive the attacker must know a valid site id; (5) no additional servlet filter outside the reviewed security XML enforces membership for /api/1/services/**.

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot as a defensive source review: 1249 source files reported by get_source_scope (no binaries excluded, no symlinks, no sensitive-name exclusions); the P1 relation index parsed 785/785 Java files (0 parse errors) but covers 1129/1249 files (120 files have no index records) and explicitly does not implement control flow, data flow, semantic resolution, or runtime/Spring enforcement verification. I inspected the REST controllers (v2), the security XMLs (api.xml/common.xml/web.xml), StudioConfiguration defaults, service facades and internal implementations (content, configuration, security/users/groups, marketplace, repository, deployment/publish, scripting, dashboard, audit), MyBatis mappers for dynamic SQL, the default-site Groovy REST scripts, and the legacy Spring Security voters/wiring. The strongest source-evidenced issue is the missing authorization on legacy API 1 deployment (bulk-golive) and the related legacy content write endpoints; one candidate submitted.
limitations: Static review only: no code, tests, server, scanner, or exploit payload was executed; no runtime behavior is confirmed.

Not all 1249 files were read line-by-line; large files such as GitContentRepository (91 KB), RepositoryManagementServiceInternalImpl (52 KB), ConfigurationServiceInternalImpl (44 KB), NotificationServiceImpl, SyncFromRepositoryTask, WorkflowServiceImpl and SearchServiceInternalImpl were reviewed selectively (searched/partially read), so additional issues may exist there.

crafter-commons validation annotations/validators (@ValidSiteId, @ValidateSecurePathParam, @SqlSort, EsapiValidator, SecurePathValidator) and the Jenkins sandbox library are external to this snapshot, so their exact enforcement semantics could not be verified; conclusions that rely on them are marked as assumptions.

The P1 index omits 120 files and provides only syntactic navigation hints (no data flow, no semantic resolution, no Spring DI/security enforcement), so index absence was not treated as evidence of safety and index labels were not treated as vulnerability verdicts.

The forgot-password e-mail template (forgotPassword.ftl) and the exact runtime mapping of /api/1/services/** to the default-site scripts are outside or only indirectly represented in this snapshot; both were treated as uncertainties rather than confirmed facts.

rejected_leads.lead: Host-header injection in the forgot-password e-mail link (EmailForgotPasswordTaskFactory captures request.getRequestURL() and puts it in the reset e-mail model together with the reset token; /api/2/users/forgot_password is public).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible token-theft vector (CWE-640), but the e-mail template (studio.security.forgotPassword.email.template = /templates/system/email/forgotPassword.ftl) is not in this snapshot, so it could not be verified that the token-bearing link is built from the attacker-influenced authoringUrl rather than the configured serviceUrl. Requires victim interaction and was kept as an unconfirmed lead instead of the primary candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Command injection in ImageMagickTransformer (Runtime.getRuntime().exec of a concatenated command line, including a config-supplied 'options' string).
rejected_leads.reason: The injected parameters come from the site asset-processing configuration (pipeline config), not from HTTP request data, so an attacker would already need configuration write access; no request-level attacker control found.

rejected_leads.lead: SQL injection through MyBatis ${sort}/${order}/${sortField.field} interpolation (AuditDAO.xml, GroupDAO.xml, UserDAO.xml, ItemDAO.xml, PublishRequestDAO.xml).
rejected_leads.reason: All call sites reviewed are guarded by @SqlSort/@ValidateStringParam whitelists at the controllers, by mapSortFields mapping to DB columns, or by int-typed parameters (${days}). crafter-commons validator internals are outside this snapshot, so residual uncertainty remains, but no reachable unvalidated path was found.

rejected_leads.lead: XSLT/XPATH injection during marketplace plugin wiring (parentXpath substituted into an XSLT template before Saxon execution).
rejected_leads.reason: Values originate from plugin descriptors obtained during plugin installation; attacker control requires install_plugins permission plus a malicious marketplace/Git plugin, and Saxon feature configuration is in the external engine/commons code. Weaker attacker model than the submitted candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: StudioContentAPIAccessDecisionVoter grants only content_read for legacy content write endpoints other than write-content.json (create-folder, rename-folder, reorder-items).
rejected_leads.reason: Verified as a real authorization gap and reported as part of the same legacy-authorization root cause in the submitted candidate (corroborating trace), not as a separate candidate.

summary: Snapshot reviewed: Crafter Studio (craftercms/studio) 4.3.0-SNAPSHOT, 1249 source files (full Java/Groovy/XML/Spring-context/script set per get_source_scope; P1 index covered 1129 files and 785/785 Java files, with 120 files absent from the index). Strongest candidate found: broken access control on the legacy API 1 endpoints. Any authenticated user can call POST /api/1/services/api/1/deployment/bulk-golive.json and queue a site's pending changes for publishing (including to the live environment) without the publish permission or even site membership, because the legacy security voters only cover /api/1/services/api/1/content/ and /api/1/services/api/1/publish/commits.json, and the underlying v1 deployment service methods carry no @HasPermission checks (their v2 counterparts do). The same legacy-authorization weakness also lets a read-only site member create/rename content via /content/create-folder.json and /content/rename-folder.json, which are granted with only content_read by StudioContentAPIAccessDecisionVoter. One candidate submitted; other leads are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
